title: Per-reanalysis datasheets + reuse/citation tracking setup
context: For the reanalysis outputs to be reusable and citable, each reanalysis needs a structured datasheet that documents provenance, license, limitations, and how to cite it. A reuse/citation tracking mechanism is also needed so the project can measure real-world adoption — a key metric for Hee-Lee Oss 'delivered, not merged'. The datasheet template should be standardized across reanalyses so the community can rely on a consistent format.
objective: Create a standardized per-reanalysis datasheet template and produce the first datasheet for the pilot reanalysis, plus set up a mechanism for tracking external reuse and citation events.
acceptanceCriteria: A standardized per-reanalysis datasheet template is defined covering: dataset accession + title, pipeline version, container digests, run manifest reference, output license (CC-BY-4.0), attribution requirements (original dataset authors, repository, reference databases), limitations, 'not medical advice' notice, and a 'how to cite' section.
The first datasheet is completed for the pilot reanalysis (pilot-009) using the template.
A mechanism for tracking external reuse and citation events is set up (e.g., a CITATION.cff file, a tracking log, or a GitHub Discussions thread), with instructions for reporters.
Datasheets are licensed CC-BY-4.0 and committed to the project repo.
resources: proteomics-reanalysis-report-011 (pilot reanalysis report to draw from)
proteomics-reanalysis-pilot-009 (run manifest reference for the pilot datasheet)
output: A committed standardized datasheet template plus the first pilot datasheet, and a reuse/citation tracking setup; licensed CC-BY-4.0.
